turns.note: First split, roughly C5/C6, to see costs and split behavior.
Build skeleton: C5/C6 split, C4/C5 split (C5 mix bottoms), C7/C8 split, C8/C9 split for octane.
Shift cut points: more boil-up in T to push C4 overhead, less in BB so heptane tops is purer, add octane/nonane column.
Add C6 paraffin/naphthene split on BT, C3/C4 split on TT, and retune heptane/octane/nonane columns via mass-balance boil-up targets.
Sharpen root (keep pentane out of bottoms), B (keep heptane out of C6 cut), make BT a hard hexane/MCP split for C6 paraffin mix, and retarget BB tops to ~315 mol/s heptane.
Go back to the best valid design to see its settings before making smaller changes.
Push pentane out of root bottoms, sharpen BT to make C6 paraffin mix (>95%), cut heptane tops to ~250 for purity, and sharpen octane toward premium.
Revert to best (turn 4) to see its stream compositions before targeted fixes (free re-evaluation).
Sharpen heptane/octane split in BB; make BT a harder paraffin/naphthene split with smaller tops to approach C6 paraffin mix.
Push residual pentane out of root bottoms (it contaminates BTT) and sharpen hexane/MCP split in BT to get BTT >95% C6 paraffins.
Revert to best (turn 9) to inspect its streams for free before targeted changes.
Sharpen root nC5/C6 split with more stages (pentane leaks into BTT) and push BT to slightly smaller, sharper tops to cut MCP, aiming BTT >95% C6 paraffin mix.
Strip pentane (~4%) out of BTT as small tops so BTTB becomes >95% C6 paraffin mix (~$650M/yr); push slightly more heptane overhead in BB so octane stream gets purer.
Push the ~66 mol/s heptane that leaks into BTB down into BB (lower B boil-up), take it overhead in BB as premium heptane, and sharpen BBB toward 99% octane premium.
Revert to best (turn 13) to inspect its streams for free before further targeted changes.
Try to get octane to premium (>99%) by sharpening BB and BBB, and test an iC5/nC5 split on TB to sell pure pentanes instead of C5 blend.
Revert to best (turn 13) to inspect its streams for free.
Recover unsold BTB (443 mol/s): strip heptane as bottoms (BTBB), then split n-hexane (tops, C6 paraffin mix) from MCP+cyclohexane (bottoms, C6 naphthene mix).
Sharpen n-hexane / MCP split in BTBT (more stages, higher reflux, lower pressure) so tops become C6 paraffin mix and bottoms C6 naphthene mix (~$500M/yr combined potential).
BTBT costs $88M and yields no sellable product; removing it should raise reward to ~3.10.
Split C5 blend into iC5 (tops) / nC5 (bottoms) for pure prices; nudge BB distillate up to remove heptane leaking into octane.
Revert to best (turn 20) to inspect its streams before attacking the unsold hexane/naphthene stream BTBT.
Instead of the hard nC6/MCP split, recover cyclohexane (bp 354 K vs MCP 345 K) as pure bottoms from BTBT (~96 mol/s, ~$190-225M/yr).
Push octane to premium (>99%): move remaining heptane overhead in BB, cut nonane in BBBT with more reflux; sharpen BTB to remove heptane from cyclohexane product.
Push BBBT octane from 98% to >99% premium (+~$160M/yr) with more stages and reflux in BBB.
Revert to best (turn 23) to inspect its streams for free before next targeted change.
Octane BBBT at 97% (2% heptane, 1% nonane): push more heptane overhead in BB via higher boil-up, and cut nonane with more reflux/stages in BBB, aiming for >99% premium.
Octane now premium but nonane bottoms at 88% (17 mol/s octane). Raise BBB boil-up to push octane up so bottoms reach ≥95% nonane, with a bit more reflux to keep tops premium.
Nonane bottoms just below 95% (5% octane): nudge BBB boil-up up. Cyclohexane bottoms has 5% heptane leaking from BTB: lower BTB boil-up so heptane stays in BTBB.
Recover the 66 mol/s of heptane in BTBB (92% heptane, 8% cyclohexane) with a small column: cyclohexane goes overhead (D≈6), heptane bottoms ≥95% (~$80M/yr).
Try splitting the unsold nC6/MCP stream (278 mol/s, ~$350M potential) in a dedicated tall low-pressure column: hexane tops (C6 paraffin/pure) and MCP bottoms.
Revert to best (turn 30, nC6/MCP column didn't pay); try pushing BBT heptane from 97% to ≥99% premium (+~$60M) with higher BB reflux.
Revert to best (turn 30) to inspect its streams; turn 32's change to BB broke octane/nonane purity.
Split the C5 mix (sold at 85% of mean price) into isopentane tops and n-pentane bottoms, which could reach pure or premium grade (+$130-280M/yr gross).
The previous C5 split was too weak, so both products still sold as C5 mix. Try a much sharper iC5/nC5 split, aiming for premium n-pentane bottoms (worth up to about +$135M/yr).
TBT is ~95% iC5 with 4% nC4 and sells only as C5 mix; push more butane overhead in T (higher boil-up) so isopentane qualifies as pure (+~$58M).
Turn 36 pushed butane into TT and ruined the C3/C4 products; revert to turn 35 best to inspect streams (free).
Strip the ~13 mol/s butane from TBT (95% iC5, sold as C5 mix) with a small column so iC5 bottoms reaches premium (+~$120M).
Push remaining nC4 out of iC5 bottoms (TBTB at 98%) to reach 99% premium (+~$65M).
Polish BBT heptane (97%, 2% octane) with a small column: strip octane to a tiny bottoms so heptane tops reaches 99% premium (+~$60M).
Octane/nonane products are 100% pure (over-purified); cut BBB reflux/boil-up to save energy cost while staying ≥99%.
BT is the most expensive column ($105M); try lower reflux/boil-up to save energy while keeping C6 paraffin blend and downstream products.
Turn 42's BT cost cut ruined the C6 paraffin blend, so go back to the turn 41 best to look at its streams (no new solves).
BTBTT (278 mol/s, 61% nC6/36% MCP) is worth nothing; try a sharp nC6/MCP superfractionator so nC6 tops gets to ≥95% and MCP+CH bottoms sells as the naphthene blend (potentially +$300M).
The BTBTT superfractionator cost $50.6M/yr and both of its products were still off-spec, so go back to the turn 41 best (no new solves) and look at its streams.
Retry nC6/MCP split with a taller, balanced (D/B≈1.8) superfractionator to recover ~$196M nC6, and split the C4 mix into iC4/nC4 pure products.
The nC6/MCP superfractionator costs $48M/yr and still leaves both products off-spec, so remove it. Keep the new iC4/nC4 split, which adds about $19M/yr net.
Turn BTBT into a direct nC6 / (MCP+CH) superfractionator, D/B≈170/201. The goal is nC6 tops ≥95% (~$196M) and MCP+CH bottoms sold as the naphthene blend (~$297M vs $135M now).
Turn 48's direct nC6/naphthene superfractionator lowered the reward to 3.342, so go back to the turn 47 best (3.543) and look at its streams.
Push iC5 (TBTB, 98%) to 99% premium: raise TB reflux to cut nC5 in its tops, and give TBT more stages and reflux to strip nC4. Also polish heptane BTBBB to premium.

BTBTT (nC6 61%/MCP 36%) is worth $0 but holds ~$340M of value. Try a very tall low-pressure superfractionator with D/B set near 170/108 (reflux 18, boil-up 30) so the nC6 tops reaches ≥95% and the MCP+CH bottoms sells as naphthene blend.
Go back to the turn 50 best (3.615) so I can look at its streams and choose the next small improvements.
BTTT loses about 21 mol/s of C6 paraffins. Shrink the tops and sharpen the cut so more C6 goes into the BTTB blend while nC5 stays low.
Lower energy in BBB (nC8/nC9) and TB (iC5/nC5) to cut cost while trying to keep premium products.
Turn 54's energy cuts lowered the reward, so go back to the turn 53 best (3.629) and look at its streams again.

Restructure the C6 section. BT cuts between nC6 and MCP, so nC6 goes to the C6 paraffin blend, which can tolerate up to 5% MCP. BTB then separates naphthenes (tops, sold as blend) from nC7, so BTBT is no longer needed.
Turn 56's restructure of the C6 section dropped the reward to 2.687, so go back to the turn 53 best (3.629) and look at its streams again.

BTBTT (nC6 61%/MCP 36%, about $340M of value) currently sells for nothing. Try a very tall, high-reflux nC6/MCP split with D/B about 168/108 to make an nC6-rich tops for sale and MCP+CH bottoms for the naphthene blend.

Stopping at 106 of 400 solves. The best design is from turn 53, scoring 3.629 (valid). The last design I evaluated (turn 58, 3.551) is not that one, but the best valid design is what counts. The one big prize left is the nC6/methylcyclopentane stream (BTBTT, worth about $340M if separated). I tried to split it three times (turns 48, 51 and 58) and moved nC6 into the C6 paraffin blend once by rebuilding the C6 section (turn 56). Every attempt lowered the reward. The two components boil only about 3 K apart, so the columns needed are too costly at these prices. Smaller tweaks, such as cutting energy use in turn 54, also made things worse. The lost streams that remain are small, so I don't expect further edits to beat 3.629.
